questions.q: When moist air is forced to rise over a mountain barrier, cools and condenses, the resulting rainfall is called:
questions.e:
Correct answer: Orographic or relief rainfall.
Key points: Orographic (relief) rainfall occurs when moist air is lifted over high ground, expands and cools, causing condensation and precipitation. Convectional rainfall is driven by surface heating; cyclonic rainfall is linked to low-pressure systems; frontal rainfall forms where air masses meet.
Why the other options are incorrect: “Convectional rainfall” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “Cyclonic rainfall” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “Frontal rainfall” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation.
Exam takeaway: Revise the key concept and distinguish it from the common distractors.

questions.q: A tax is described as progressive when:
o: The average tax rate falls as taxable income rises
Everyone pays the same total amount
The average tax rate rises as taxable income rises
The tax rate is always zero below every income level
questions.e:
Correct answer: The average tax rate rises as taxable income rises.
Key points: Under a progressive tax structure, the average tax rate increases as taxable income rises. A proportional tax keeps the rate constant, while a regressive structure can make the average burden fall as income rises. Do not confuse a higher marginal rate on an income band with the average rate on all income.
Why the other options are incorrect: “The average tax rate falls as taxable income rises” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “Everyone pays the same total amount” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “The tax rate is always zero below every income level” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation.
Exam takeaway: Revise the key concept and distinguish it from the common distractors.
Source: NCERT textbook portal — introductory economics — https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.q: A shop marks an item at ₹2,400 and gives a 15% discount. What is the selling price?
questions.e:
Correct answer: ₹2,040.
Key points: Formula: Discount = Marked Price × Discount rate ÷ 100. Substitution: ₹2,400 × 15 ÷ 100 = ₹360. Selling price = ₹2,400 − ₹360 = ₹2,040. Shortcut: after a 15% discount, pay 85% of the marked price: 0.85 × ₹2,400 = ₹2,040. The other options do not equal the marked price minus ₹360.
Why the other options are incorrect: “₹2,060” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “₹2,160” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “₹2,280” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation.
Exam takeaway: Revise the key concept and distinguish it from the common distractors.
Source: Original quantitative-aptitude practice; arithmetic independently checked — https://ssc.gov.in/

questions.q: What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.e:
Correct answer: ₹2,100.
Key points: Formula: Amount A = P(1 + r/100)^t. Substitution: A = ₹10,000(1.10)^2 = ₹10,000 × 1.21 = ₹12,100. Compound interest = A − P = ₹12,100 − ₹10,000 = ₹2,100. Quick check: first-year interest is ₹1,000; second-year interest is 10% of ₹11,000 = ₹1,100; total = ₹2,100.
Why the other options are incorrect: “₹2,000” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “₹2,200” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “₹1,000” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation.
Exam takeaway: Revise the key concept and distinguish it from the common distractors.
Source: Original quantitative-aptitude practice; arithmetic independently checked — https://ssc.gov.in/

questions.q: A person is 7th from the left and 12th from the right in the same row. How many people are in the row?
questions.e:
Correct answer: 18.
Key points: When a person’s position is counted from both ends, total people = left position + right position − 1 because the person is counted twice. Calculation: 7 + 12 − 1 = 18. Do not simply add 7 and 12; subtract one to avoid double-counting the person.
Why the other options are incorrect: “17” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “19” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “20” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation.
Exam takeaway: Revise the key concept and distinguish it from the common distractors.

questions.q: A person walks 5 km north, then 3 km east, and then 5 km south. Where is the person relative to the starting point?

questions.q: A 12 V potential difference is applied across a 3 Ω resistor. What current flows through it, assuming an ideal resistor?
questions.e:
Correct answer: 4 A.
Key points: Ohm’s law: V = IR, therefore I = V/R. Substitute V = 12 V and R = 3 Ω: I = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 A. Unit check: volt per ohm equals ampere. The other options do not satisfy V = IR for these values.
Why the other options are incorrect: “3 A” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “9 A” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “36 A” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation.
Exam takeaway: Revise the key concept and distinguish it from the common distractors.
Source: NCERT textbook portal — electricity — https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

Why the other options are incorrect: “Encrypts every file on a computer” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “Creates user passwords” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “Measures available RAM” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation.

questions.q: How many characters are in a regular taxpayer’s GST Identification Number (GSTIN)?
questions.e:
Correct answer: 15.
Key points: A GSTIN has 15 characters: the first two represent the state code; the next ten correspond to the PAN; the 13th identifies the entity under that PAN in the state; the 14th is normally “Z”; and the 15th is a checksum character. The other lengths are incorrect.
Why the other options are incorrect: “10” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “12” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation; “16” is incorrect because it does not fit the stated fact, definition or calculation.
Exam takeaway: Revise the key concept and distinguish it from the common distractors.
